items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Oh, him and Peter Bocard then used to play together on those parades.

ctx.x: Oh, him and Peter Bocard then used to play together on those parades. I think it was the... I think Solastain had a brass band at that time, and they were playing together, and he was a member of the band. But I didn't like that. You didn't like that? No, I didn't like that. Couldn't get me out there. I didn't want to play. Now, sometime when a musician would die like that, or René and them would get together and just build up a band. No pay, just play behind him, you know what I mean? I'd go out there, something…
How long were you with Tom Alvin? How many years?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-15
items.q: And they had another fellow here called Peter Bocard and his bunch.

ctx.x: Did you say P-Ron would play for a special class of people though, huh?

Yeah, he played for the better class of people, see. He played for the doctors and the lawyers and people up here on St. Charles Street, people back in the place and all that kind of people, the higher class of people, see. And they liked that sweet music and slow and waltzes a lot of things, you know, something like that. Well, the average band around here didn't play that, see. Like John Robeshoe and P-Ron. And they had another fellow here called Peter Bocard and his bunch. Now they played all that kind of…
He had a good band. I had a good band.
